author: Agatha Christie
plan_notes: Lean deterministic plan: per-chapter targets apportioned by source-word share; extradiegetic chapters excluded. No prepass, no signature enumeration.

signatures.passage_hint: Cut your losses. Time’s merciful. You’ll forget.

signatures.passage_hint: but I _loved_ her. I’d have given the soul out of my body to save her from harm.
signatures.why: Tommy's emotional climax; the emphasis matters.

signatures.passage_hint: It was her I saw talking to Whittington at that nursing home in Bournemouth. She wasn’t a patient there! She was a nurse!
signatures.why: Julius's recognition that the Manchester 'Jane' was the Bournemouth nurse.

signatures.passage_hint: It’s mighty lucky you did say it.
signatures.why: Ambiguous reaction; leaves Julius's intentions open.

signatures.passage_hint: What on earth was a photograph of the French girl Annette doing in Julius Hersheimmer’s writing-table?
signatures.why: Chapter-ending hook; exact wording essential.

segments.title: TOMMY MAKES A DISCOVERY

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXII. IN DOWNING STREET

signatures.passage_hint: that girl at Manchester was just a plant.
signatures.why: Tommy's key reversal in his own letter voice.

signatures.passage_hint: she’s no more drowned than I am.
signatures.why: Characteristic phrasing of his conclusion.

signatures.passage_hint: _But if they know that the papers have been recovered by us_, neither of those two girls’ lives will be worth an hour’s purchase.
signatures.why: The reason for the sealed envelope.

signatures.passage_hint: He hasn’t got any--so he’s difficult to deceive.
signatures.why: Carter's character judgment of Tommy, which is thematically central.

signatures.passage_hint: But I sometimes fancy I see a shadow behind.
signatures.why: Ironic misdirection about Sir James.

signatures.passage_hint: Come at once, Astley Priors, Gatehouse, Kent. Great developments--TOMMY.
signatures.why: The original telegram text.

signatures.passage_hint: “Perhaps it never left it,” suggested the lawyer gently.
signatures.why: Insinuation against Julius; exact gentle phrasing.

signatures.passage_hint: “The darned fool!” he murmured.
signatures.why: Ambiguous end beat.

segments.title: IN DOWNING STREET

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXIII. A RACE AGAINST TIME

signatures.passage_hint: At the pictures the crooks always have a restoorant in the Underworld.
signatures.why: Albert's cinema-fed voice.

signatures.passage_hint: “This is a one-man show,” said Tommy to himself. “The thing to do is to get hold of the man.”
signatures.why: Tommy's thesis, which is borne out later.

signatures.passage_hint: You can see that I’m a Soldier by my feet
signatures.why: The signal song.

signatures.passage_hint: only, as it happened, the butler was Whittington!
signatures.why: Comic-reveal sting.

signatures.passage_hint: if the spider lets the fly walk out too easily, the fly might suspect it was a put-up job.
signatures.why: Tommy's insight into the trap.

signatures.passage_hint: “TWOPENCE.”
signatures.why: The crucial planted clue; exact spelling.

signatures.passage_hint: “Yes, a damned fool,” he said softly. “But so’s some one else! And at last I know who it is!”
signatures.why: Chapter-ending hook; no name may be given.

segments.title: A RACE AGAINST TIME

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXIV. JULIUS TAKES A HAND

signatures.passage_hint: “Hands up--or I shoot!”
signatures.why: Abrupt tonal switch from drawl to threat; the turning point of the scene.

signatures.passage_hint: I did not know it until afterwards. He was one of a crowd.
signatures.why: Fair-play clue that Brown is unremarkable and was hidden in plain sight.

signatures.passage_hint: Maybe he’ll send some flowers to the funeral, but _you_ won’t smell them!
signatures.why: Julius's signature gallows-humour countdown.

signatures.passage_hint: using the words that have created many unnecessary panics
signatures.why: Narrator's dry ironic aside; voice marker.

signatures.passage_hint: I persuaded him to come on the trip for his health.
signatures.why: Comic understatement in Julius's voice.

signatures.passage_hint: But it’s the one real and original Jane Finn we’ve got here.
signatures.why: Identity revelation of Annette, in Julius's idiom.

signatures.passage_hint: I guess there’s nothing wrong with your memory. Been fooling them all the time, eh?
signatures.why: Reveals that Jane's amnesia was a sham; sets up Chapter XXV.

signatures.passage_hint: “Dry up! I want a few words with you, Mr. Julius Hersheimmer.”
signatures.why: Cliffhanger; its ambiguity must stay intact.

segments.title: JULIUS TAKES A HAND

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXV. JANE’S STORY

signatures.passage_hint: It’s just an idea that came into my head a long time ago. Tommy’s got it too--I’m almost sure he has.
signatures.why: Tuppence's withheld suspicion; ambiguous about its target.

signatures.passage_hint: and as he did so he _winked_....
signatures.why: The chilling small detail of Jane's narrative.

signatures.passage_hint: Then I opened my eyes and started babbling in _French!_
signatures.why: The pivot of Jane's bluff; links to 'Annette'.

signatures.passage_hint: His voice was very ordinary and quiet, but somehow, I don’t know why, he scared me worse than the woman.
signatures.why: Fair-play clue to the nondescript Mr. Brown.

signatures.passage_hint: _And the magazine was still rolled up in the pocket!_
signatures.why: Suspense beat over where the papers are.

signatures.passage_hint: I knew the others would think I meant Mrs. Vandemeyer, but I hoped it might make Mr. Beresford think of the picture.
signatures.why: Explains the Marguerite cry.

signatures.passage_hint: _for it is Mr. Brown’s plan that we are to lead him_.
signatures.why: Sir James's double-edged statement, sinister in hindsight.

signatures.passage_hint: “No, Miss Finn,” said Sir James unexpectedly. “Not your cousin.
signatures.why: Chapter-ending bombshell.

segments.title: JANE’S STORY

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXVI. MR. BROWN

signatures.passage_hint: Since then he had been hand and glove with those sworn to hunt him down.
signatures.why: Ironically true of the speaker himself.

signatures.passage_hint: Bullets fly--but don’t hit anybody.
signatures.why: Sir James's theory, quietly contradicted by Julius's graze.

signatures.passage_hint: “Because Julius Hersheimmer is Mr. Brown,” said Sir James dryly.
signatures.why: The false assertion stated flatly before the reversal.

signatures.passage_hint: “In this room.... You don’t understand? _I am Mr. Brown_....”
signatures.why: The climactic reveal; keep the exact pacing.

signatures.passage_hint: So no one will think of searching the pockets of Sir James Peel Edgerton!
signatures.why: Brown's gloating plan in his own words.

signatures.passage_hint: “Checkmate to the Young Adventurers,” he said
signatures.why: Chess motif; the villain's flourish.

signatures.passage_hint: “‘_Ave, Cæsar! te morituri salutant_,’” he said, still looking at Tommy.
signatures.why: His last words and grandiose self-image.

signatures.passage_hint: whilst an odour of bitter almonds filled the air.
signatures.why: Death by poison, rendered indirectly.

segments.title: MR. BROWN

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXVII. A SUPPER PARTY AT THE _SAVOY_

signatures.passage_hint: “Morally, I shall always consider I have been jilted!”
signatures.why: Tuppence's comic dignity; resolves the proposal.

signatures.passage_hint: She’d never spell her name ‘Twopence,’ but anyone who’d never seen it written might quite easily do so.
signatures.why: Payoff of the signature clue.

signatures.passage_hint: “We all kept back something or other,” said Tuppence thoughtfully.
signatures.why: Thematic summary of withheld knowledge.

signatures.passage_hint: Personality! I put it on like a glove!
signatures.why: Brown's method in his own voice.

signatures.passage_hint: There are hundreds of men called Brown--there are hundreds of men looking just like me....
signatures.why: Ties to the nonentity / crowd motif.

signatures.passage_hint: He is not clever, but it is hard to blind his eyes to facts....
signatures.why: Villain's verdict on Tommy; key character judgment.

signatures.passage_hint: “A great man,” he said. “Genius, or insanity, who can say?”
signatures.why: Carter's ambivalent epitaph.

signatures.passage_hint: “I will give you a toast. The Joint Venture which has so amply justified itself by success!”
signatures.why: Closes the book-long joint-venture motif.

segments.title: A SUPPER PARTY AT THE _SAVOY_

segments.raw_heading: CHAPTER XXVIII. AND AFTER

signatures.passage_hint: “I love you now, Julius,” said Jane Finn. “I loved you that first moment in the car when the bullet grazed your cheek....”
signatures.why: Jane's acceptance and its callback to the rescue; the trailing ellipsis carries the romantic beat.

signatures.passage_hint: “From all the things Tuppence didn’t say!”
signatures.why: Signature ironic insight into Tuppence's concealed feeling.

signatures.passage_hint: with a singular lack of originality, was also returning to the _Ritz_ via Regent’s Park.
signatures.why: Narrator's wry aside that parallels the two couples.

signatures.passage_hint: “You’re not going to marry him, do you hear?” he said dictatorially.
signatures.why: Tommy's comic jealous explosion breaking the constraint.

signatures.passage_hint: “But I suppose you prefer sterling worth,” said Tuppence demurely.
signatures.why: Tuppence's teasing self-reference, which prompts Tommy's inarticulate admission.

signatures.passage_hint: “You think I mind saying it, but I don’t in the least! _Ours_, so there!”
signatures.why: Tuppence's oblique proposal; the emphasis on _Ours_ is the climax.

signatures.passage_hint: “A sport!”
signatures.why: Final redefinition of marriage that closes the book's motif.

signatures.passage_hint: “And a damned good sport too,” said Tommy.
signatures.why: The book's last line.

segments.title: AND AFTER
